subdomain: 5.5 Address ethical AI considerations (bias, fairness, transparency)

en.question: An optional skills-course recommender no longer receives an explicit age field. It still uses graduation year, historical course participation, and manager ratings. Older workers receive fewer suitable recommendations in a reviewed sample. The team claims age-related bias is now impossible. What is the best next step?

options.text: Assess proxy inputs and label quality against job-relevant criteria; test subgroup errors and mitigations in this deployment.
options.note: Removing an explicit attribute does not remove correlated inputs or biased upstream labels. Contextual analysis can distinguish legitimate task information from mechanisms producing unfair recommendations.

options.text: Remove age labels from evaluation records as well, making the training and evaluation pipelines equally blind to the attribute.
options.note: Eliminating evaluation visibility does not establish that proxies have no effect. It can prevent the team from detecting and measuring the reported disparity.

options.text: Drop every feature statistically correlated with age and declare the remaining system fair without further outcome evaluation.
options.note: Correlation alone does not determine task relevance or capture every source of disparity. A blanket feature-removal rule is not evidence that the resulting recommendations are fair.

options.text: Attribute the disparity to manager ratings and retain them unchanged, treating human-produced ratings as inherently neutral evidence.
options.note: Human-produced labels can reflect historical selection or assessment bias. Their origin does not establish neutrality or remove the need to examine recommendation errors.
